svg.title: Part 1 The anatomy of a case

div.style: width: 1920px; height: 1080px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 80px 120px; background: #F4F5F7; color: #11151B; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 36px
display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 22px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #4A5361

div.h2: Four files, and who reads each
div.p: Open the vendored copy of a published case under shared/contract/cwa/conformance/cases/.

svg.aria-label: case.json holds the id, rules and description. snapshot.json is the frozen input. expected.trace.json is the trace a conformant assembler emits. expected.payload.txt is the rendered bytes, absent for a refusal. A rejection has only case.json and snapshot.json. Checkpoint 1 below.

g.text: id, the requirement ids it exercises (rules), one sentence
the frozen input, valid against snapshot.schema.json
the trace a conformant assembler emits, trace_id and timings aside
the rendered bytes, compared byte for byte
absent when the case expects a refusal
It breaks exactly one snapshot check;
f-tie escalates and is surfaced: two leaders, same producer,
For the clock to decide: freshness_tiebreak true, one leader strictly later.
A refusal has no expected.payload.txt; R-17: a refused assembly
